question: What is the main use of an ultrasonic cleaner in the CSSD?

options.A: Killing bacterial spores using high heat
options.B: Removing microscopic debris using sound waves
options.C: Applying a protective rust-proof coating
options.D: Drying moisture from surgical hinges

explanation: Ultrasonic cleaners use high-frequency sound waves to create tiny scrubbing bubbles that blast hidden dirt out of tiny instrument hinges and joints.

question: Why is the first few weeks after birth a critical time to watch new mothers closely?

options.A: Severe complications like heavy bleeding and infections happen most often then
options.B: Hormone levels drop to zero immediately after birth
options.C: Babies cry constantly during the first few days
options.D: Mothers are usually discharged before labor pain stops completely

explanation: You've got this! Life-threatening emergencies such as heavy bleeding (hemorrhage) and infections are most common right after delivery, which is why close nursing monitoring is so essential. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h1)

question: A woman at home experiences heavy vaginal bleeding shortly after delivering the placenta. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.A: Send a family member to buy oral iron supplements from a local shop
options.B: Wait for thirty minutes to see if the bleeding stops on its own
options.C: Perform immediate uterine massage and administer oxytocin
options.D: Document the estimated blood loss in the register

explanation: Uterine massage and uterotonic drugs stimulate contractions to clamp down open blood vessels and stop the bleeding immediately. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h4)

question: At what angle should the head of the bed typically be elevated to help prevent ventilator-associated pneumonia?

options.A: 15 degrees downward
options.B: 90 degrees upright
options.C: 30 to 45 degrees
options.D: 0 degrees flat

explanation: Elevating the head of the bed uses gravity to stop stomach contents and oral secretions from sliding down into the lungs. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T4#GNS321_U2_T4_h5)

question: How is the malaria parasite (Plasmodium) most commonly spread in Nigeria?

options.A: Inhalation of airborne droplets
options.B: Bite of the female Anopheles mosquito
options.C: Ingestion of poorly washed vegetables
options.D: Direct person-to-person skin contact

explanation: You've got this! Infected female Anopheles mosquitoes carry the malaria parasite and pass it into the bloodstream when they bite.

question: Why is smoking a cigarette near oxygen therapy a massive fire hazard?

options.A: Smokers are unable to handle oxygen equipment properly
options.B: Oxygen tanks release toxic gases when heated by smoke
options.C: Cigarettes automatically explode when they touch oxygen tubing
options.D: Oxygen feeds fires and makes flames spread with explosive speed

explanation: Medical oxygen makes fires burn super fast and extremely hot. Even a small spark near oxygen can turn into a dangerous blaze instantly.

question: What patient position is standard and most appropriate for inserting a rectal suppository?

options.A: Upright sitting position in a chair
options.B: Prone position lying flat on the stomach
options.C: Sims position on the left side
options.D: Flat on the back with legs held high

explanation: The Sims position naturally aligns with the downward curve of the sigmoid colon and rectum, making insertion easier. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T18#GNS125_U3_T18_h7)

question: A student looks at a slide where bone-building cells (osteoblasts) are laying down matrix directly into a tissue sheet. What process is happening?

options.A: Intramembranous ossification
options.B: Interstitial bone growth
options.C: Endochondral ossification
options.D: Articular cartilage repair

explanation: Spot on! When bone forms straight from a connective tissue sheet without a cartilage stage, it's called intramembranous ossification.

question: In which zone of the surgical suite can staff members wear regular street clothes?

options.A: Sterile core zone
options.B: Restricted zone
options.C: Unrestricted zone
options.D: Semi-restricted zone

explanation: The unrestricted zone is the welcome area where you enter before changing into your scrubs. Easy peasy!

question: Why is effective nutrition counselling more than just handing a patient a printed diet sheet?

options.A: It requires understanding the patient's daily life and financial limits.
options.B: Patients in rural communities usually cannot read printed materials.
options.C: Doctors are the only ones legally allowed to explain diet sheets.
options.D: Printed sheets are too expensive to produce in local clinics.

explanation: Real dietary guidance must fit a patient's actual living conditions, budget, and access to local food markets rather than being a generic list. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T20#GNS214_U1_T20_h1)

question: When does avoiding conflict turn into a real problem on a nursing unit?

options.A: When it is used during a fire drill or sudden cardiac arrest
options.B: When it is used for five minutes to let a colleague catch their breath
options.C: When it is used permanently to sweep serious problems under the rug
options.D: When it is applied to trivial, unimportant daily annoyances

explanation: Using avoidance as a permanent habit just hides serious issues until they blow up later. Problems need to be faced eventually!

question: Why do cat bites easily cause deep joint or tendon infections?

options.A: Cats secrete a local anesthetic that hides the pain of the bite
options.B: Cat saliva naturally resists all standard antibiotic treatments
options.C: Cat teeth are sharp and slender, pushing bacteria deep into tight tissues
options.D: Cats possess venom glands located near their salivary ducts

explanation: Think of a cat's teeth like tiny needles. They puncture deep beneath the skin, depositing bacteria right into sterile spaces like joints and tendons.

question: Why must a nurse always make sure a water-soluble lubricant is used for a proctoscopy?

options.A: To prevent the light source from overheating inside the rectum
options.B: To sterilize the metal components of privacy equipment instantly
options.C: To act as a strong local anesthetic agent for the rectal walls
options.D: To ease smooth passage through the anal sphincter without harming tissue

explanation: Great choice! Water-soluble jelly reduces friction so the scope slides in comfortably without hurting the patient, and it washes away easily afterward.

question: A clinic wants to run a reproductive health campaign that teenagers will actually trust. Who should they partner with first?

options.A: International trade unions
options.B: Federal revenue agencies
options.C: Youth-led organizations
options.D: Hospital security guards

explanation: Spot on! Youth groups rock at peer-to-peer connection, making them brilliant at reaching young people who might stay away from formal clinics.

question: What actually happens to the prostate gland in benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH)?

options.A: Non-cancerous cell overgrowth
options.B: Infection-driven tissue necrosis
options.C: Malignant tumor invasion
options.D: Fibrotic tissue shrinking

explanation: Spot on! 'Benign' means non-cancerous. In BPH, the prostate cells simply overgrow, which is very common as men age.

question: Why is nebulization often chosen over other inhalers for patients in acute respiratory distress?

options.A: It requires only normal, quiet breathing instead of a deep, forced inhalation.
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for any vital sign monitoring.
options.C: It stops all lung infections within minutes of starting the treatment.
options.D: It works ten times faster than any intravenous medication available.

explanation: Patients struggling to catch their breath cannot coordinate deep inhalers, making normal breathing through a nebulizer mask much easier. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h1)

question: Which skin preparation practice is essential before performing an intraarticular puncture?

options.A: Applying warm lotion to soften the skin surface
options.B: Shaving the entire limb hair without any cleanser
options.C: Wiping the skin clean with a dry cotton ball only
options.D: Allowing the antiseptic solution to dry completely on the skin

explanation: Antiseptic agents need time to dry so they can fully kill microbes on the skin surface before the needle enters. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h6)

question: Which body system is most commonly involved when studying paroxysmal disorders like epilepsy?

options.A: The renal filtration system
options.B: The gastrointestinal tract
options.C: The integumentary system
options.D: The central nervous system

explanation: Most classic paroxysmal disorders, such as seizures, originate from sudden electrical disruptions in the brain. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T16#GNS222_U3_T16_h1)

question: What is the best way to talk to a patient who has trouble communicating after a stroke?

options.A: Always finish their sentences if they take longer than two seconds
options.B: Ask simple yes-or-no questions and give them time to answer
options.C: Speak very loudly and quickly to keep their attention focused
options.D: Communicate only through written notes to avoid frustration

explanation: Giving them time and keeping questions simple takes the pressure off and makes chatting much easier.

question: What is caregiver burnout?

options.A: An allergic reaction to cleaning supplies used in the home
options.B: Physical and emotional exhaustion caused by prolonged caregiving stress
options.C: A sudden medical illness caught from a patient in the hospital
options.D: The legal termination of a home health care contract

explanation: Caregiver burnout happens when family or informal caregivers become overwhelmed by the continuous physical and emotional demands of supporting a relative. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T4#GNS324_U5_T4_h4)

question: What is the leading chronic health condition that results in lower limb amputation?

options.A: Rheumatoid arthritis
options.B: Chronic bronchitis
options.C: Essential hypertension
options.D: Diabetes mellitus

explanation: Diabetes damages blood vessels and nerves over time, making wounds hard to heal and often leading to tissue death. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T12#GNS324_U4_T12_h1)

question: A patient on a water pill (diuretic) keeps waking up all through the night. Why is this happening?

options.A: The drug stimulates brain activity like caffeine
options.B: The medicine makes the patient urinate frequently
options.C: The medication causes severe joint pain
options.D: The pill induces sudden anxiety attacks

explanation: Diuretics make the kidneys produce more urine. Naturally, this means the patient has to make frequent trips to the restroom at night!

question: Why does our sense of taste naturally react strongly against bitter foods?

options.A: To identify energy-rich carbohydrate sources
options.B: To maintain normal blood electrolyte levels
options.C: To signal the presence of dietary protein
options.D: To warn the body against potential poisons

explanation: Think of bitterness as your body's built-in alarm system! It evolved to help us spot dangerous toxins or plant alkaloids before we swallow them.

question: When would you as a nurse request a backrest device for your patient?

options.A: To protect the heels from rubbing against the mattress
options.B: To assist with upper body elevation for breathing or eating
options.C: To raise the entire bed frame higher off the floor
options.D: To keep the lower legs straight and immobilized

explanation: Correct! Backrests support the back and shoulders in a comfortable sitting position, making it much easier for the patient to eat, drink, or breathe.

question: A patient has severe burns on 40% of their body. Which skin job will be seriously affected?

options.A: Filtering blood plasma
options.B: Digesting dietary fats
options.C: Producing red blood cells
options.D: Making vitamin D

explanation: You got it! Since healthy skin is needed to make vitamin D from sunlight, extensive burns make this process very difficult. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h6)

question: Why is taking corticosteroids together with NSAIDs (like ibuprofen) a big risk?

options.A: It causes blood pressure to drop dangerously low.
options.B: It cancels out the steroid so it doesn't work.
options.C: It greatly increases the chance of stomach ulcers and bleeding.
options.D: It stops the liver from filtering other drugs.

explanation: Brilliant! Both drugs irritate the stomach lining. Combining them multiplies the risk of painful ulcers and internal bleeding.

question: Which amino acid is the starting point for making catecholamines and thyroid hormones?

options.A: Alanine
options.B: Tyrosine
options.C: Glycine
options.D: Tryptophan

explanation: Tyrosine is the key building block amino acid used to manufacture important hormones like adrenaline and your thyroid hormones. One step at a time, you're learning it!

question: Why do we need to make sure we have enough trained staff before starting a health program?

options.A: To guarantee that administrative tasks take precedence over patient care
options.B: To fulfill a legal requirement set by international donor agencies
options.C: To ensure the workforce can handle the service volume without burning out
options.D: To prevent the community from ever questioning clinical decisions

explanation: Matching your team size to the expected crowd keeps patients happy and protects our hardworking nurses from burnout.

question: Why is a psychosocial assessment vital for clients with neurologic conditions?

options.A: Nerve damage and brain injury affect thinking, mood, and daily life.
options.B: It is the only legal way to discharge a patient from the hospital.
options.C: Physical therapy cannot start until mental health is fully cured.
options.D: It replaces the need for a standard physical doctor's examination.

explanation: Brain and nerve disorders directly alter a person's behavior, emotions, and interactions, making psychosocial evaluation just as important as physical care. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T5#GNS222_U3_T5_h1)

question: What happens to the foetal skull bones during the process of molding?

options.A: They compress tightly and overlap each other
options.B: They dissolve temporarily under pelvic pressure
options.C: They expand outward to make the head rounder
options.D: They fracture completely to ease delivery

explanation: Molding is the natural overlapping of un-fused cranial bones to help the head adjust to the shape of the birth canal. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T16#GNS121_U6_T16_h1)

question: Why is it important to ask patients about traditional herbal remedies before giving hospital medications?

options.A: Herbal mixtures can interact dangerously with prescribed hospital medications
options.B: Traditional remedies cancel out the cost of hospital drugs
options.C: Doctors use herbal history to calculate exact body weight
options.D: Hospital management requires a complete inventory of home items

explanation: Many patients mix local herbs with hospital drugs. Asking helps you catch sneaky drug-herb reactions that could harm the patient.

question: Why does a nurse use the back of the hand when checking skin temperature over a swollen joint?

options.A: It is required by standard infection control guidelines for wound care
options.B: The skin on the dorsal hand is thinner and more sensitive to temperature changes
options.C: It prevents the patient from feeling intimidated by a direct palm touch
options.D: The palm is too warm to detect minor differences in body heat

explanation: The thin skin on the back of the hand is much better at detecting subtle variations in local skin warmth. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T3#GNS222_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why do we give emergency epinephrine into the thigh muscle instead of the arm?

options.A: The drug is absorbed much faster into the bloodstream from the thigh
options.B: The skin on the thigh feels less pain
options.C: Arm muscles are too small for emergency drugs
options.D: It stops the patient from seeing the needle

explanation: The vastus lateralis muscle in the thigh has great blood flow, helping the epinephrine get to work as fast as possible when every second counts.

question: What is the main feature of a generalized tonic-clonic seizure?

options.A: Muscle stiffening followed by rhythmic jerking
options.B: A brief moment of staring blankly into space
options.C: Localized numbness in a single fingertip
options.D: Sudden temporary paralysis of one leg

explanation: A tonic-clonic seizure has two main parts: the 'tonic' phase where the body stiffens, and the 'clonic' phase where it rhythmically jerks.

question: Why do nurses usually keep the head of the bed slightly elevated for a patient with high brain pressure?

options.A: To allow clearer visibility during frequent neurological checks
options.B: To help blood drain away from the head and lower pressure
options.C: To make it easier for the patient to swallow saliva safely
options.D: To prevent the lungs from collapsing during mechanical ventilation

explanation: Gravity is our friend here! Elevating the head helps blood flow smoothly out of the brain, keeping intracranial pressure down.

question: Why must personal distress be present alongside physical symptoms to diagnose female sexual dysfunction?

options.A: Physical symptoms alone always resolve spontaneously
options.B: Insurance companies will not pay for treatment otherwise
options.C: It proves the dysfunction is purely psychological
options.D: Some women experience variations in response without feeling bothered by them

explanation: Great thinking! Every body is different. What feels like a problem to one person might be completely normal and comfortable for another, which is why personal distress matters.

question: Why must high-risk heart patients take antibiotics before certain dental procedures?

options.A: Dental manipulation can introduce bacteria into the bloodstream, which may latch onto damaged heart valves.
options.B: Dental medications frequently interact negatively with cardiac drugs like digoxin.
options.C: Tooth decay directly causes inflammation of the outer pericardial sac.
options.D: Local anesthetics used by dentists weaken the heart muscle permanently.

explanation: Gum bleeding during dental work lets mouth bacteria sneak into the bloodstream. For a vulnerable heart, prophylactic antibiotics act like a shield!

question: Why can a dry mouth quickly lead to infections and tooth decay?

options.A: Saliva maintains a high body temperature inside the mouth
options.B: Saliva contains antimicrobial agents and washes away harmful bacteria
options.C: Saliva hardens the tooth enamel against physical impact
options.D: Saliva produces white blood cells that fight off gum disease

explanation: Think of saliva as your mouth's natural cleaning and defense system—it washes away food and fights germs with protective proteins.

question: A patient is diagnosed with a tumor growing in the smooth muscle of the thigh. Which classification applies best?

options.A: Sarcoma
options.B: Carcinoma
options.C: Lymphoma
options.D: Leukemia

explanation: Connective and supportive tissues like muscle, bone, and fat give rise to sarcomas rather than carcinomas. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T6#GNS321_U1_T6_h4)

question: What is a major environmental hazard in hospital corridors?

options.A: Soft carpeted flooring
options.B: Too many bright windows
options.C: Clutter and blocked pathways
options.D: Excessive room ventilation

explanation: Leaving equipment or boxes in hospital hallways creates clear tripping hazards for staff, visitors, and vulnerable patients. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h2)

question: A patient tells you they feel extremely panicked and short of breath at the thought of entering a narrow, enclosed scanner. What is your best first action?

options.A: Tell the patient to close their eyes and ignore the fear
options.B: Cancel the appointment permanently without consulting anyone
options.C: Force the patient into the scanner quickly to get it over with
options.D: Acknowledge the fear and report the need for an anti-anxiety medication order

explanation: You're a caring nurse! Validating their fear and helping arrange for medication or an open MRI makes the experience much better.

question: How does cutting back on coffee and energy drinks help a patient dealing with an anxiety disorder?

options.A: It prevents central nervous system stimulation that mimics anxiety symptoms
options.B: It guarantees uninterrupted sleep for twelve hours every night
options.C: It acts as a powerful direct replacement for antidepressant medication
options.D: It cures the genetic predisposition linked to panic disorder

explanation: Correct! Caffeine is a stimulant that causes jitteriness and a fast pulse—things you definitely don't need when managing anxiety. Smart choice!

question: Knowing the exact classification and drug-resistance profile of an infecting organism directly helps the nurse do what?

options.A: Determining the patient's expected hospital discharge date
options.B: Administering targeted antimicrobial therapy effectively
options.C: Calculating the patient's exact daily fluid intake
options.D: Choosing the correct hospital room wall paint color

explanation: When you know the exact bug and what drugs it hates, the medical team can prescribe the precise medication to knock it out quickly and safely.

question: How does carbon dioxide travel away from the fetus?

options.A: It travels through the maternal lymphatic system only
options.B: It diffuses across the placental membrane into maternal blood
options.C: It is stored safely inside the amniotic fluid until birth
options.D: It is actively pumped out by the umbilical arteries

explanation: CO2 is a small molecule that easily slips (diffuses) right across the membrane from the baby's tiny blood vessels into the mother's blood to be breathed out by her lungs. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T5#GNS121_U6_T5_h4)

question: What is a major source of information when conducting a retrospective nursing study?

options.A: New clinical trials
options.B: Electronic health records
options.C: Live patient interviews
options.D: Real-time vital sign tracking

explanation: Correct! Since retrospective research relies on things that already happened, electronic health records (EHRs) are a goldmine for this kind of data.

question: What is the main thing that happens in neoplasia?

options.A: Uncontrolled and uncoordinated cellular proliferation
options.B: Rapid healing of acute tissue damage
options.C: Temporary swelling caused by local infection
options.D: Normal replacement of dead skin cells

explanation: Think of neoplasia as new growth that just won't quit! The cells keep multiplying without listening to the body's normal stop signals.

question: What is the main reason we apply most topical drugs to the skin?

options.A: To bypass the digestive tract entirely for rapid blood concentration
options.B: To achieve a localized effect at the application site
options.C: To provide systemic nutrition through the skin
options.D: To replace intravenous therapy in emergency resuscitation

explanation: You've got this! Topical medications are designed to work right where you put them, treating local skin issues without flooding the whole body with medicine.

question: A patient sits crying silently in bed after receiving a terminal diagnosis. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Turn on the television to distract them from sadness
options.B: Remind them that modern medicine is very advanced
options.C: Leave the room immediately to give them privacy
options.D: Sit quietly beside the patient and offer a reassuring touch

explanation: Offering presence and gentle touch shows support and lets the patient know they are not alone in their grief. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T8#GNS321_U4_T8_h6)

question: What does 'intrinsic sphincter deficiency' mean?

options.A: Blockage of urine flow by the prostate gland
options.B: Damage or weakness of the urethral sphincter muscle itself
options.C: A temporary infection lining the urinary tract
options.D: Overactivity of the main bladder muscle

explanation: Simply put, the valve muscle itself has lost some of its strength and can no longer seal tightly on its own.

question: What is the main pressure that pushes fluid through the kidney's filter?

options.A: Osmotic pull from red blood cells
options.B: Active transport by tubule cells
options.C: Ciliary action inside Bowman's capsule
options.D: Hydrostatic pressure in the capillaries

explanation: You got it! The natural blood pressure inside those tiny capillaries pushes water and small nutrients across the filter, just like a sieve.

question: Why is it important to document the exact number of shocks the AED delivered during a code?

options.A: It tells the biomedical department when to throw away the machine's battery.
options.B: It provides critical data for the medical team reviewing the patient's clinical course.
options.C: It proves to the hospital administration that the nurse followed the correct protocol.
options.D: It determines how much financial charge the patient receives for equipment use.

explanation: Doctors and the healthcare team need to know how many shocks were given to understand how the patient's heart responded and plan their next steps.

question: What clinical sign typically tells the clinician that the uterine cavity is successfully emptied during MVA?

options.A: The syringe plunger automatically pushes itself back
options.B: The patient falls into a deep sleep
options.C: Fluid turns completely clear without any blood bubbles
options.D: Bright red foam appears and a gritty feeling is sensed

explanation: When tissue is cleared, the canula comes into contact with the empty uterine wall, producing a characteristic gritty sound or feel along with red foam in the tubing. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h5)

question: What is the most common early sign of endometrial cancer?

options.A: Postmenopausal vaginal bleeding
options.B: Swelling in both lower legs
options.C: Severe lower back pain
options.D: Rapid unintended weight loss

explanation: You nailed it! Any bleeding or spotting after menopause is a red flag that always needs a doctor's attention.

question: What change typically happens inside the fallopian tubes after a severe infection heals?

options.A: Replacement of tubal tissue with normal ovarian follicles
options.B: Complete regeneration of healthy, unimpeded mucosal cilia
options.C: Permanent widening and increased muscular strength of the walls
options.D: Fibrous scar bands and adhesions that obstruct the lumen

explanation: Just like a skin wound leaves a scar, healing inside the delicate tubes creates fibrous bands that can narrow or block the passage.

question: Which symptom is most characteristic of circulatory overload during a blood transfusion?

options.A: Shortness of breath and crackles in the lungs
options.B: Sudden widespread hives and severe skin itching
options.C: High fever accompanied by uncontrollable shivering
options.D: Sharp pain radiating into the lower back area

explanation: Circulatory overload occurs when fluid volume overwhelms the heart, leading to pulmonary congestion and breathing difficulty. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T8#GNS123_U2_T8_h7)

question: What does disease 'eradication' mean in public health?

options.A: Lowering local cases to an acceptable level
options.B: Eliminating a disease from one specific country
options.C: Permanent reduction to zero of worldwide incidence
options.D: Stopping an outbreak in a single hospital ward

explanation: You've got this! Eradication means the disease is completely wiped out across the entire globe, so we never have to fight it again. Smallpox is a great example!

question: What goes wrong in the body to cause the symptoms of multiple sclerosis (MS)?

options.A: Accumulation of beta-amyloid plaques in the temporal lobes
options.B: Excessive release of glutamate causing immediate excitotoxicity
options.C: Thrombus formation blocking blood flow in the middle cerebral artery
options.D: Autoimmune destruction of central nervous system myelin

explanation: In MS, the body's immune system mistakenly attacks and strips away the protective myelin coating on nerve fibers, slowing down signals.

question: A mum's partograph has crossed past the action line. What is your best next step?

options.A: Wait another four hours to see if labour picks up speed on its own.
options.B: Initiate definitive medical or surgical interventions immediately.
options.C: Stop monitoring vital signs to reduce patient anxiety.
options.D: Discharge the patient home since labour is progressing slowly.

explanation: You've got it! Crossing the action line means labour is in danger territory. Action must be taken, like medical augmentation or preparing for theatre.

question: Why is the postpartum uterine cavity so easily invaded by bacteria?

options.A: Gastric acid production increases significantly during labor
options.B: The cervix remains completely dilated for several months
options.C: Normal flora inside the uterus becomes entirely pathogenic
options.D: The placental site is a large, raw, vascular wound

explanation: Think of where the placenta detached—it leaves behind a large, healing wound with open blood vessels. This makes it a very easy pathway for bacteria to enter.

question: What is the main job of the fluid found inside the protective sac around the heart (pericardium)?

options.A: To store extra blood volume during times of heavy exercise
options.B: To provide extra oxygen directly to the outer heart muscle
options.C: To reduce friction as the heart beats against surrounding tissues
options.D: To prevent electrical signals from leaving the heart wall

explanation: Your heart beats thousands of times a day without stopping! The pericardial fluid acts like a slippery lubricant so the heart can glide smoothly inside the chest without irritation.

question: According to Rubin's maternal role theory, what is the first major task an expectant mother focuses on?

options.A: Ensuring safe passage for herself and her child
options.B: Rejection of her own childhood parenting style
options.C: Immediate financial planning for college
options.D: Complete isolation from social networks

explanation: Spot on. Keeping herself and the baby safe and healthy is always the number one early priority for an expectant mum.

question: Why do doctors check blood calcium and PTH levels at the same time?

options.A: To determine if the thyroid gland is producing too much thyroxine
options.B: To check if the patient has an active bacterial infection in the blood
options.C: To calculate the exact glomerular filtration rate of both kidneys
options.D: To see if the parathyroid gland's hormone response matches the calcium level

explanation: Comparing PTH and calcium together helps clinicians figure out if a calcium problem is actually coming from a misbehaving parathyroid gland.

question: What is your best first step if a painful bruise (hematoma) starts swelling up while you are trying to find a vein?

options.A: Remove the tourniquet and withdraw the needle at once
options.B: Apply an ice pack directly over the needle while it remains inside
options.C: Push the needle deeper to secure better placement in the vein
options.D: Leave the tourniquet tight and attach a larger vacuum tube

explanation: If a hematoma starts forming, stop right away! Remove the tourniquet and pull out the needle to keep the patient comfortable and prevent more bleeding under the skin.

question: In which of these situations is it UNSAFE to give standard anti-bleeding drugs?

options.A: Recent deep vein thrombosis (DVT)
options.B: Severe surgical bleeding
options.C: Mild hemophilia A flare-up
options.D: Accidental warfarin overdose

explanation: A deep vein thrombosis means a clot is already stuck where it shouldn't be. Adding an anti-bleeding drug here puts the patient at high risk.

question: Where in the brain do generalized seizures start?

options.A: A localized spot in one hemisphere
options.B: Only the frontal lobe
options.C: The brainstem exclusively
options.D: Both hemispheres simultaneously

explanation: Well done! Generalized seizures involve electrical activity spreading across both sides of the brain right from the start.

question: A clinic nurse wants to stop teenage girls from dropping out of school due to menstrual hygiene challenges. What is the most practical community action?

options.A: Advise all young girls to stay home during their menstrual periods
options.B: Provide free sanitary pads and educate both girls and community members on menstrual management
options.C: Report the affected families to the federal ministry of education for neglect
options.D: Recommend that local schools close down entirely during rainy seasons

explanation: Providing pads and open education removes the shame and practical barriers that make girls miss school. Simple solutions go a long way in public health!

question: Why is checking out the home environment so important for a patient's nutrition?

options.A: It guarantees the patient will eat all prescribed meals
options.B: It reveals practical barriers like trouble with grocery shopping
options.C: It proves whether the family is hiding food from the patient
options.D: It replaces the need to check the patient's weight

explanation: Exactly! Home visits show you real-life challenges, like physical issues that make buying or cooking food hard.

question: What is a normal finding right after Gallows traction is removed?

options.A: Complete loss of feeling in both legs
options.B: One leg suddenly growing longer than the other
options.C: Running and walking right away without help
options.D: Stiffness in the hips and knees from lying still

explanation: Keeping those little legs up in the air for weeks makes the joints stiff. Gentle stretching and movement will get them back to normal in no time!

question: What electrical change happens inside the cell to spark a smell signal?

options.A: An influx of sodium and calcium ions into the cell
options.B: A sudden drop in cyclic AMP levels
options.C: The direct breakdown of protein molecules
options.D: A massive outflow of potassium ions

explanation: Correct! When ion channels open, positively charged sodium and calcium ions rush inside the cell. This change in electrical charge creates an impulse that travels up to the brain.

question: A patient comes in with a suspected blood clot in their leg vein (deep vein thrombosis). What scan will the doctor likely order?

options.A: Renal B-Mode ultrasound
options.B: Pelvic M-Mode ultrasound
options.C: Cardiac echocardiogram
options.D: Vascular Doppler ultrasound

explanation: A vascular Doppler scan is specifically designed to peek inside blood vessels and catch clots early.

question: How does drug absorption in the lower rectum affect metabolism?

options.A: It sends all medications directly to the stomach
options.B: It destroys the active ingredients instantly
options.C: It forces the drug to be stored in the kidneys
options.D: It bypasses the liver's first-pass metabolism

explanation: Lower rectal veins carry the drug straight into the general circulation, skipping the quick breakdown by the liver that oral pills face.

question: Why is maintaining the cold chain so crucial in immunization programs?

options.A: To prevent temperature-sensitive vaccines from losing their potency
options.B: To prevent theft of medical supplies by unauthorized personnel
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of transporting heavy medical equipment
options.D: To keep the vaccines frozen solid until the exact moment of injection

explanation: Well done! Vaccines need strict temperature control to stay active. If the cold chain breaks, the medicine won't work.

question: Why do we need a multi-sectoral approach (involving health, legal, and community groups) to eliminate FGM in Nigeria?

options.A: Foreign donors refuse to fund local healthcare workers
options.B: Federal laws ban NGOs from working in rural areas
options.C: Traditional rulers want total control over all medical and school policies
options.D: No single strategy alone can tackle such deep-rooted social and legal barriers

explanation: Brilliant! Because FGM touches on culture, law, health, and social norms, lasting change requires a teamwork approach across laws, healthcare, and local communities.

question: Which healthcare professional specializes in testing hearing and fitting hearing aids?

options.A: Ophthalmologist
options.B: Audiologist
options.C: Dietitian
options.D: Podiatrist

explanation: An audiologist is the expert you call for hearing tests, ear diagnoses, and finding the right hearing devices for patients. Easy to remember!

question: What is the main goal of collecting data in nursing research?

options.A: To replace the need for physical patient assessments
options.B: To punish staff who do not follow hospital rules
options.C: To gather information for answering research questions
options.D: To increase the cost of running healthcare facilities

explanation: Spot on! We collect data systematically so we can find clear answers to our research questions and ultimately improve patient care.

question: Why is an erection that lasts over four hours (priapism) a medical emergency?

options.A: It results in permanent loss of bladder control
options.B: It triggers rapid systemic hypertension
options.C: It causes immediate rupture of the urethra
options.D: It leads to permanent damage from trapped, oxygen-depleted blood

explanation: When blood gets stuck without fresh circulation coming in, the tissues are starved of oxygen and can suffer permanent damage very quickly. Fast action is key!

question: How does progesterone help protect an early pregnancy?

options.A: By stimulating the rapid shedding of the endometrial lining
options.B: By causing a sudden drop in core body temperature
options.C: By stopping all pituitary hormone release
options.D: By relaxing uterine smooth muscle to prevent early contractions

explanation: Progesterone acts like a calming agent for the uterus, keeping the muscles relaxed so a newly implanted embryo can stay safe and secure.

question: Why should a DRF pricing strategy include an inflation buffer?

options.A: To discourage patients from buying unnecessary medications
options.B: To pay for the transport costs of delivering emergency care
options.C: To generate bonus income for the hospital management board
options.D: To ensure future re-stocking can cover rising market prices

explanation: You've got it! Prices in the market go up. Adding a small inflation buffer ensures that when you need to buy a new batch of drugs, you'll actually have enough money to afford them.

question: Which cells in the stomach lining make hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor?

options.A: Parietal cells
options.B: Mucous neck cells
options.C: G cells
options.D: Chief cells

explanation: Spot on! Parietal cells are the stomach's acid factories. They also make intrinsic factor, which your body needs to absorb vitamin B12 properly.

question: What is the approximate weight of a normal term human placenta?

options.A: About 500 grams
options.B: About 100 grams
options.C: About 2,000 grams
options.D: About 1,500 grams

explanation: A healthy term placenta typically weighs around 500 grams, serving as the metabolic bridge between mother and fetus. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T6#GNS121_U6_T6_h1)

question: What imaging test is considered the absolute gold standard for spotting a pituitary tumor?

options.A: An ultrasound scan of the blood vessels in the neck
options.B: A plain X-ray picture of the skull from the side
options.C: A standard CT scan of the head without any contrast dye
options.D: An MRI of the brain using contrast dye

explanation: MRI is the best choice because it gives super clear pictures of soft tissues. This lets doctors spot tiny adenomas and see if they are crowding nearby structures like the optic nerves.

question: How is a 'confirmed' case different from a 'suspected' case?

options.A: A confirmed case requires no medical isolation, unlike a suspected case
options.B: A suspected case means the patient has fully recovered from the illness
options.C: A suspected case is always more severe and infectious than a confirmed case
options.D: A confirmed case has laboratory proof of the pathogen, while a suspected case only has symptoms

explanation: Spot on! Lab results turn a 'suspected' case (based only on signs and symptoms) into a 'confirmed' case.

question: What baseline assessment is most critical to perform and record before starting a gastric lavage?

options.A: Abdominal skin turgor and color tone
options.B: Recent dietary history for the past week
options.C: Vital signs and neurological status
options.D: Detailed psychological background history

explanation: Recording baseline vitals and mental status allows the nurse to monitor for rapid changes caused by toxin absorption or procedural complications like vagal stimulation. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h4)

question: What is the primary reason for choosing soap and water over alcohol rub?

options.A: Soap and water dry out the skin much faster
options.B: Hands are visibly soiled or contaminated with spore-forming germs
options.C: Alcohol rubs are too expensive to use in general wards
options.D: Alcohol rubs take longer to apply than washing

explanation: Visible dirt and certain tough bacterial spores require the physical scrubbing action of soap, water, and friction to be removed. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical problem caused by poorly planned, excessive protein intake?

options.A: Potential for chronic constipation due to low fiber
options.B: Extra workload for the kidneys
options.C: Immediate development of type 1 diabetes
options.D: Increased risk of dehydration

explanation: Type 1 diabetes is an autoimmune condition where the body attacks its own insulin-making cells—it isn't caused by eating too much steak or beans!

question: What is a major benefit of good teamwork and communication on a ward?

options.A: It eliminates the need for patient medical records
options.B: It ensures nurses never have to speak with doctors
options.C: It allows the ward to close earlier every evening
options.D: It helps prevent medical errors and streamlines treatment

explanation: Spot on! When doctors, nurses, and other health workers talk clearly, everyone stays on the same page and mistakes are easily avoided.

question: Why must a nurse use a filter needle when drawing medication from a glass ampoule?

options.A: To make the plunger move more smoothly inside the barrel
options.B: To filter out bacteria present in the room air
options.C: To change the chemical pH of the liquid medicine
options.D: To prevent tiny glass shards from entering the syringe

explanation: Snapping the neck of a glass ampoule creates microscopic shards. A filter needle traps these fragments so they are not injected into the patient. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T22#GNS122_U1_T22_h4)

question: At what point does the second stage of labour officially start?

options.A: When the placenta is delivered
options.B: When the cervix is completely dilated
options.C: When the amniotic membranes rupture
options.D: When contractions become painful and regular

explanation: You nailed it! The second stage begins right when the cervix is fully open at 10 cm and ends when the baby is born.

question: Why is a functional assessment necessary when caring for someone with a physical disability?

options.A: To prove that the patient is unable to walk
options.B: To diagnose the original cause of the injury
options.C: To determine the financial cost of hospital equipment
options.D: To match nursing interventions with the patient's actual capabilities

explanation: Assessing what a patient can still do prevents nurses from doing tasks the patient is fully capable of managing themselves. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T10#GNS225_U5_T10_h1)

question: How do GBV survivors often present when they first walk into a healthcare clinic?

options.A: By demanding immediate admission to the intensive care unit
options.B: By immediately handing the triage nurse a written police report
options.C: With vague physical complaints like chronic headaches or abdominal pain
options.D: With clear, detailed accounts of the assault upon entering the room

explanation: Because of fear or shame, survivors often don't speak up right away. They might just complain of body pains or headaches, making gentle nursing assessment key!

question: What is a major problem when a hospital runs on a strictly punitive (blame-heavy) culture?

options.A: Errors are driven underground out of fear of punishment
options.B: Clinical outcomes improve because mistakes stop happening
options.C: Employee innovation and creativity increase significantly
options.D: Staff members report mistakes immediately and openly

explanation: If staff know they will be heavily punished for minor mistakes, they will hide them instead of reporting them. This stops the team from learning and keeps patients unsafe!

question: How do fluoroquinolone antibiotics mainly stop bacteria from growing?

options.A: By blocking human protein production
options.B: By dissolving the outer bacterial capsule
options.C: By stopping bacterial DNA from copying
options.D: By changing the pH of the blood plasma

explanation: These drugs target the specific machinery bacteria use to copy their genetic material, stopping them right in their tracks.

question: What essential check must a nurse perform immediately after removing an IV catheter?

options.A: Rinse the puncture site with cold tap water
options.B: Measure the exact volume of blood left in the hub
options.C: Soak the removed plastic tubing in an antiseptic jar
options.D: Inspect the catheter tip to ensure it is fully intact

explanation: Checking the tip confirms that no broken plastic piece remains inside the patient's vein. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h9)

question: What is the medical term for inflammation of the fallopian tubes?

options.A: Endometritis
options.B: Cervicitis
options.C: Salpingitis
options.D: Oophoritis

explanation: Salpingitis simply means infection and inflammation in one or both of the fallopian tubes. You've got this!

question: Why should you keep a client's neck straight and in a neutral position when managing high ICP?

options.A: Straight necks make it easier for the client to chew their meals
options.B: It keeps the breathing tube securely taped to the side of the mouth
options.C: It prevents the client from accidentally pulling out their intravenous lines
options.D: Bending the neck can kink jugular veins and trap blood in the head

explanation: Great to know for clinicals! Twisting or bending the neck blocks blood from draining out of the brain, causing it to back up and shoot up the intracranial pressure.

question: Where in the body is Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone (GnRH) originally manufactured?

options.A: The hypothalamus
options.B: The adrenal medulla
options.C: The gonads
options.D: The anterior pituitary

explanation: Correct! Special nerve cells tucked inside the hypothalamus build and release GnRH to kickstart the whole reproductive cascade.

question: What is the main problem in the body when someone has anaemia?

options.A: Increased thickness of the blood plasma
options.B: Rapid destruction of blood platelets
options.C: Too many white blood cells
options.D: Reduced oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood

explanation: You've got this! Anaemia simply means the blood doesn't have enough red blood cells or hemoglobin to carry the oxygen your body needs to function well.

question: What is the main role of the government when partnering with voluntary health agencies?

options.A: Providing policy frameworks and regulatory oversight
options.B: Operating every single rural clinic without assistance
options.C: Stopping all foreign funding from entering the country
options.D: Handling all grassroots community mobilization directly

explanation: Correct! The government sets the rules, guidelines, and policies so everyone working in healthcare stays aligned and safe.

question: Why is it important to interview a patient suspected of experiencing GBV alone, without family members present?

options.A: To comply with visiting hour restrictions set by hospital management
options.B: To prevent family members from asking questions about medical costs
options.C: To ensure the patient feels safe to speak honestly without fear of retaliation
options.D: To save time during busy hospital shift change periods

explanation: Abusive partners or controlling family members may intimidate the patient, preventing them from disclosing the truth if they remain in the room. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T9#GNS312_U4_T9_h7)

question: Why do patients with poorly controlled diabetes often develop delayed stomach emptying (gastroparesis)?

options.A: High sugar levels destroy specific gut cells through sudden local infections
options.B: Excess sugar physically coats the stomach lining and blocks food
options.C: High blood sugar damages the nerves (like the vagus nerve) that tell stomach muscles to move
options.D: Diabetes causes the stomach to make too much mucus, slowing digestion down

explanation: Over time, high blood sugar harms delicate nerves around the body. When the vagus nerve gets damaged, it can't send proper signals to make the stomach muscles contract.

question: When you try to straighten a patient's arm, it resists you and feels very stiff. What is this finding called?

options.A: Ataxia
options.B: Clonus
options.C: Flaccidity
options.D: Spasticity

explanation: Spasticity is when muscles feel tight and resist being stretched quickly. It happens when upper motor pathways in the nervous system are injured.

question: Why are weight-bearing joints like the knees and hips so prone to physical stress?

options.A: They rely only on skin and fat for stability
options.B: They lack any form of cartilage protection
options.C: They must support body weight while managing movement forces
options.D: They are completely fused and cannot absorb shock

explanation: Exactly! Our knees and hips carry gravity's load all day while taking the pounding of walking and running, leading to natural wear over time.

question: A pregnant patient reports severe chest pain spreading down her left arm. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Report it immediately for cardiac evaluation
options.B: Suggest she take a strong antacid tablet right away
options.C: Reassure her that this is normal third-trimester heartburn
options.D: Advise her to lie down and drink cold milk

explanation: Chest pain spreading to the arm is a red flag for the heart! Never brush it off as simple heartburn.

question: What is the very first step a nurse should take after sustaining a needle stick injury while on duty?

options.A: Hide the incident from the supervisor to avoid paperwork
options.B: Report the incident immediately for evaluation and prophylaxis
options.C: Soak the injured finger in cold river water
options.D: Take a strong painkiller and finish the remaining shift

explanation: Always report immediately! Quick action allows the occupational health team to give you prompt counseling and protective meds.

question: Why do community health nurses spend time educating the public?

options.A: To replace formal school teachers in local primary classrooms
options.B: To empower individuals and groups with knowledge to prevent illness
options.C: To test public speaking skills during routine ward rounds
options.D: To fulfill mandatory administrative writing quotas

explanation: Spot on! Education is one of our most powerful tools. When people understand how diseases spread and how to live healthily, they can take charge of their own wellbeing.

question: What is the main difference between decorticate and decerebrate posturing when scoring motor response?

options.A: Decorticate involves abnormal flexion inward, while decerebrate involves rigid extension outward
options.B: Decorticate affects only the legs, while decerebrate affects only the arms

options.D: Decorticate means the patient obeys commands, while decerebrate means they make no sound

question: A nurse manager has limited funds for a ward. Which item should be bought first to keep patients safe?

options.A: Essential life-saving medications and functional oxygen supplies
options.B: Upgraded entertainment systems for the staff break room
options.C: Foreign travel allowances for senior administrative staff members
options.D: Expensive decorative furniture for the manager's private office

explanation: Patient care always comes first! When funds are tight, life-saving drugs and oxygen take priority over office luxuries every single time.

question: Why must health education topics change as children grow older?

options.A: Because older students refuse to study basic hygiene practices
options.B: To ensure teachers do not repeat the exact same lesson plan
options.C: To match the developmental stage and emerging life challenges of the students
options.D: Because younger children cannot understand the human body

explanation: Spot on! Topics like personal growth or reproductive health need to be introduced at the right age so students can truly relate to and apply them.

question: What is considered the single most effective habit to stop the spread of infection?

options.A: Changing hospital scrubs hourly
options.B: Proper hand hygiene
options.C: Wearing sterile gloves all day
options.D: Using strong chemical sprays

explanation: Good old handwashing (or using alcohol rub) at the right moments is your absolute best defense against spreading germs!

question: When taking off your personal protective equipment (doffing), which item should come off FIRST?

options.A: Gloves
options.B: Isolation gown
options.C: Respirator mask
options.D: Face shield

explanation: Spot on! Your gloves are the dirtiest item since they touched the patient directly, so peeling them off first keeps the rest of your cleanup process safe.

question: When a blood vessel gets injured, what is the correct order of the steps your body takes to stop bleeding?

options.A: Coagulation, vascular spasm, platelet plug formation
options.B: Platelet plug formation, coagulation, vascular spasm
options.C: Vascular spasm, platelet plug formation, coagulation
options.D: Coagulation, fibrinolysis, vascular spasm

explanation: Great thinking! First, the vessel squeezes tight (spasm), then platelets rush in to patch the hole (plug), and finally, the clotting proteins seal it up solid (coagulation).

question: What is the main goal of doing a slit-lamp examination?

options.A: To wash out dust from the lower eyelid
options.B: To get a close-up, magnified view of the front of the eye
options.C: To measure exact distance vision
options.D: To check the patient's full side vision

explanation: The slit-lamp shines a bright, magnified light on front eye structures like the cornea, iris, and lens so you can see them clearly.

question: In which section of the fallopian tube does fertilization usually occur?

options.A: Ampulla
options.B: Fimbriae

options.D: Cervix

question: How does an infant acquire natural passive immunity from their mother?

options.A: Through receiving routine childhood routine immunizations

options.C: By inheriting active immune memory cells during conception
options.D: Through the transfer of maternal antibodies via breast milk

explanation: Maternal antibodies pass to the baby across the placenta and through breast milk, giving the newborn temporary protection against common infections. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h2)

question: What is widely recognized as one of the biggest threats to public health in any population?

options.A: Excessive availability of public park spaces
options.B: Strict enforcement of local sanitation laws
options.C: Widespread poverty and economic instability
options.D: High levels of cultural diversity in neighborhoods

explanation: Poverty makes it super hard for people to afford basic needs like good food, shelter, and healthcare, which naturally drags down health outcomes.

question: Why is the left anterior descending (LAD) artery famously called the widow-maker?

options.A: It carries deoxygenated blood back to the lungs.

options.C: It supplies blood to the major pumping walls of the left ventricle.
options.D: It controls the electrical rhythm of the heart valves.

explanation: Spot on! The LAD feeds the thick, heavy-duty walls of the left ventricle. If it gets blocked, the heart's main pumping power is severely crippled.

question: How does political corruption directly hurt maternal and child health programs?

options.A: By building more primary healthcare centers
options.B: By diverting essential medical supplies and funds meant for public clinics
options.C: By lowering the cost of prescription drugs for pregnant women
options.D: By increasing the number of trained midwives in rural villages

explanation: Corruption steals resources meant for the sick, leaving public clinics without basic drugs, working equipment, or safe spaces for mothers. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h5)

question: What is your very first action if a patient's neurological condition suddenly and unexpectedly worsens?

options.A: Ask a family member to monitor the patient for an hour
options.B: Administer a sleeping pill to help the patient rest
options.C: Notify the healthcare provider immediately and report the changes
options.D: Wait until the end of the shift to write it in the main chart

explanation: Sudden neuro changes are an emergency. Quick reporting saves lives, so always alert the doctor or senior nurse right away.

question: What is a major benefit of a man attending antenatal care visits with his partner?

options.A: He replaces the midwife during delivery
options.B: He can perform the physical examination himself
options.C: He learns about pregnancy danger signs and birth preparedness
options.D: He receives free medications for chronic illnesses

explanation: Attending antenatal visits helps fathers understand what complications to watch out for and how to prepare for emergencies. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h3)

question: What is a primary nursing responsibility regarding equipment preparation for ophthalmoscopy?

options.A: Checking battery power and light brightness on the ophthalmoscope

options.C: Sterilizing the handle and head of the device in an autoclave machine
options.D: Replacing the handheld lens with a digital camera attachment

explanation: The nurse must verify that the handheld scope has working batteries and sufficient illumination before the clinician begins the exam. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h4)

question: How do traffickers sometimes misuse the cultural practice of child fostering?

options.A: It completely stops children from ever attending primary school
options.B: It forces children to migrate permanently to foreign countries
options.C: It forces parents to pay high taxes to the local government
options.D: It is used as a cover to traffic children into domestic servitude

explanation: Traffickers disguise modern-day slavery as traditional family fostering to fool trusting parents and communities.

question: Why do newborn babies need a vitamin K injection right after birth?

options.A: Breast milk contains zero traces of fat-soluble vitamins
options.B: Their liver is too large to process normal dietary proteins
options.C: Their sterile gut cannot yet synthesize the vitamin for blood clotting
options.D: They lose all stored maternal clotting factors during delivery

explanation: A newborn's tummy is completely sterile at first, meaning they don't have the gut bacteria needed to make vitamin K yet. The shot protects them from bleeding until their gut matures.

question: A patient with advanced terminal cervical cancer is in severe, constant pain in her pelvis and back. What is your top nursing priority?

options.A: Preparing the patient for emergency radical pelvic surgery
options.B: Encouraging the patient to walk outside to distract her from the pain
options.C: Administering prescribed analgesics regularly based on pain assessment
options.D: Restricting fluid intake to decrease pressure on the pelvic organs

explanation: You've got it. In palliative care, keeping the patient comfortable through regular, structured pain relief is a top priority to preserve their dignity and quality of life.

question: What triggers the release of oxytocin during breastfeeding?

options.A: High levels of circulating estrogen
options.B: Emptying of the axillary lymph nodes
options.C: Stretching of Cooper's ligaments
options.D: Infant suckling at the nipple

explanation: Nerve signals from the nipple travel to the brain when a baby suckles, triggering the posterior pituitary to release oxytocin for milk ejection. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T16#GNS121_U5_T16_h8)

question: What important advice should you give a patient given a 10-day course of antibiotics for strep throat?

options.A: Crush the tablets and mix them with cold fruit juice
options.B: Finish all the pills even if you feel completely better
options.C: Stop taking the medication as soon as your sore throat stops
options.D: Double the next dose if you miss a single pill

explanation: Spot on! Always encourage patients to finish every single pill. Stopping early can let the strongest bacteria bounce back and cause drug resistance.

question: What is the medical name for nearsightedness?

options.A: Hyperopia
options.B: Myopia
options.C: Presbyopia
options.D: Astigmatism

explanation: Myopia means you can see things close up clearly, but far-away objects look blurry because light focuses just short of the retina.

question: Why do our veins need a system of one-way valves?

options.A: To handle high-pressure surges from the heart pumping
options.B: To filter waste products out of red blood cells
options.C: To pump blood directly into the left side of the heart
options.D: To push blood against gravity back toward the heart

explanation: Blood in veins travels under low pressure, especially from your legs climbing back up. One-way valves act like little trapdoors that stop it from slipping backward!

question: Which instrument is commonly used to gently grasp and pull out an implant rod during a removal procedure?

options.A: Large surgical scissors
options.B: A standard syringe needle
options.C: An orthopedic bone saw
options.D: Mosquito forceps

explanation: Sterile mosquito forceps are the nurse's best friend here—they provide just the right grip to gently ease the rod out through a tiny skin opening.

question: What is the main goal of sperm capacitation?

options.A: To slow down the swimming speed of the sperm
options.B: To increase the total number of chromosomes in the sperm head
options.C: To prepare the sperm membrane and enhance its ability to fertilize the oocyte
options.D: To help the sperm attach securely to the vaginal wall

explanation: Spot on! Capacitation is basically the maturation process inside the female tract that gets the sperm ready to do the job.

question: Why might a family living in severe poverty choose not to spend money on transport to a family planning clinic?

options.A: Hospitals do not allow poor people inside
options.B: Medical clinics only open during midnight hours
options.C: They prefer buying luxury items for their home
options.D: Immediate daily survival needs take priority over preventive care

explanation: Exactly. When daily food and shelter are a struggle, spending scarce cash on transport for health checkups has to wait.

question: Why is daily foot care and inspection so crucial for patients with diabetes?

options.A: Daily observation increases blood circulation to the toes
options.B: Sweat buildup guarantees the rapid development of gangrene
options.C: Nerve damage can prevent them from feeling minor cuts or blisters
options.D: Skin color changes indicate the exact blood sugar level

explanation: Diabetes can cause nerve damage (neuropathy) in the feet, meaning minor sores can go unnoticed and turn into major wounds if not checked daily. Essential nursing wisdom!

question: Why are interactive methods like role-play preferred over lecturing for school health instruction?

options.A: They guarantee that students will never fall ill
options.B: They require no preparation from the classroom teacher
options.C: Children prefer reading long medical textbooks
options.D: They actively engage students and improve practical habits

explanation: Interactive learning helps students internalize concepts and apply them to real-life situations better than passive listening. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h4)

question: How do Nucleoside Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitors (NRTIs) help fight HIV?

options.A: They dissolve the fatty outer envelope of the virus
options.B: They act as faulty building blocks to stop viral DNA creation
options.C: They physically block the outer cell membrane receptors
options.D: They destroy mature viral particles circulating in the plasma

explanation: Brilliant! NRTIs act like fake Lego pieces. When the virus tries to build its DNA, it grabs the fake piece and the process grinds to a halt.

question: What keeps a Foley catheter securely in place inside the bladder?

options.A: A flexible wire attached to the belly wall
options.B: External adhesive tape on the thigh
options.C: Natural suction created by the drainage bag
options.D: A water-filled balloon at the tip

question: On day four after delivery, a breastfeeding mother tells you she feels overwhelmed and cries easily when the baby fusses, but she loves holding her baby and sleeps well when the baby sleeps. What is your best response?

options.A: Inform her that she shows classic signs of postpartum psychosis
options.B: Tell her to stop breastfeeding immediately to stabilize her hormones
options.C: Reassure her that these feelings are common postpartum blues and will likely pass soon
options.D: Immediately arrange an emergency psychiatric admission for depression

question: What is a major fear that stops many patients from sharing their HIV status with family?

options.A: Fear of mandatory blood transfusions
options.B: Fear of losing their ability to speak
options.C: Fear of rejection and social blame
options.D: Fear of receiving free medical care

explanation: Exactly. Worry about how loved ones will react and judge them is a heavy emotional barrier for many patients.

question: Which of these is NOT a safe thing to do when giving a patient nail care?

options.A: Washing the feet with warm water
options.B: Rounding down the deep corners of toenails
options.C: Filing fingernails straight across
options.D: Inspecting the skin between the toes
