question: Why would a doctor choose a tracheostomy instead of keeping a breathing tube through the mouth long-term?

options.A: It completely stops any risk of getting an infection
options.B: It means you never have to clean around the site or use suction
options.C: It is much more comfortable and safer for long-term breathing support
options.D: It is much faster to do in an outdoor emergency

explanation: Having a tube taped through the mouth for weeks can damage the vocal cords and mouth. A tracheostomy provides a secure, comfortable airway right through the neck for patients who need long-term help.

question: A patient states they have smoked for twenty years and wonders if quitting will even help now. What is the most accurate nursing response?

options.A: Smoking only affects your lungs, not your heart or blood vessels
options.B: You must stop all at once without any help or replacement products for it to work
options.C: Quitting will benefit your heart immediately, cutting your heart disease risk in half within one year
options.D: The damage is already permanent, so quitting will not change your risk level

explanation: Cardiovascular benefits begin almost immediately after quitting smoking, and within twelve months, the excess risk of coronary heart disease drops by fifty percent. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical side effect of immune checkpoint inhibitors?

options.A: Inflammation of the colon leading to severe diarrhea
options.B: Immune-mediated pneumonitis causing breathing difficulties
options.C: Permanent structural damage to the heart muscle valves
options.D: Dermatitis and itchy rashes across the skin surface

explanation: You got this right! These drugs ramp up the immune system, causing inflammatory side effects like rashes or gut issues, but heart valve destruction isn't a hallmark of this class.

question: What is the main goal of using the 'teach-back' method after educating a patient?

options.A: To fulfill a legal requirement for signing surgical consent forms
options.B: To allow the nurse to take a break while the patient teaches the class
options.C: To test the patient's long-term memory for academic medical trivia
options.D: To have the patient explain instructions in their own words to verify understanding

explanation: Teach-back isn't testing the patient—it's testing *us*. If they can explain it back easily, you know your teaching hit the mark!

question: What is the best position for a patient during a standard lumbar puncture?

options.A: Sitting straight upright with arms down
options.B: Lateral fetal position
options.C: Prone face down on pillows
options.D: Flat on the back with legs straight

explanation: You nailed it! Curling up on the side like a fetus opens up the spaces between the back bones.

question: Why is carbidopa combined with levodopa when treating Parkinson's disease?

options.A: To cure the underlying viral infection causing the nervous disorder
options.B: To directly stimulate dopamine receptors in the skeletal muscles
options.C: To lower the patient's blood pressure during physical therapy
options.D: To prevent peripheral breakdown of levodopa before it reaches the brain

explanation: Carbidopa acts as a bodyguard for levodopa outside the brain, protecting it so it survives the journey to where it's truly needed.

question: What simple comfort measure can a nurse suggest for a patient experiencing mild fibroid cramps?

options.A: Applying a heating pad to the lower abdomen
options.B: Drinking large quantities of ice-cold water
options.C: Lying completely flat on the back for hours
options.D: Engaging in high-impact aerobic exercise

explanation: Heat helps relax the tight uterine muscles, offering a wonderful, drug-free way to soothe mild cramping.

question: Which agency plays a massive role in rolling out national immunization campaigns down to local communities?

options.A: Federal Inland Revenue Service
options.B: National Primary Health Care Development Agency
options.C: Nigerian Tourism Development Corporation
options.D: Federal Ministry of Works and Housing

explanation: You nailed it! The NPHCDA is the key driver behind primary healthcare support and nationwide vaccination drives in Nigeria.

question: What blood vessel carries oxygenated blood from the placenta back to the fetus?

options.A: Umbilical vein
options.B: Ductus venosus
options.C: Spiral endometrial artery
options.D: Umbilical artery

explanation: The umbilical vein is responsible for carrying freshly oxygenated and nutrient-rich blood from the placental villi back to the fetal circulation. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T7#GNS121_U6_T7_h1)

question: When should you apply a cold pack (cryotherapy) to a patient?

options.A: During the acute phase to reduce swelling and numb pain
options.B: To relax tight chronic muscles before a long walk
options.C: To relieve pressure on the spine from a herniated disc
options.D: To increase local blood flow in a healing chronic wound

explanation: Think of cold as a quick calmer for fresh injuries—it slows down blood flow to keep swelling down and numbs the area so it hurts less.

question: In the GATHER counseling model for family planning, what does the letter 'G' stand for?

options.A: Greet the client and establish rapport
options.B: Guarantee zero side effects to users
options.C: Give all prescription drugs immediately
options.D: Gather laboratory test results first

explanation: Correct! Good nursing care starts with a warm welcome to put the client at ease and build a trusting relationship.

question: What is the main reason iron supplements are routinely given to pregnant women?

options.A: To harden the fetal tooth enamel before delivery occurs
options.B: To prevent anemia caused by expanding blood volume and fetal demands
options.C: To lower maternal blood pressure during the third trimester
options.D: To speed up the digestion of complex proteins in the stomach

explanation: Because a pregnant mum's blood volume shoots up, her body needs extra iron to build all those extra red blood cells without running low.

question: What is the main job of rhodopsin inside rod cells?

options.A: Keeping the lens clear and flexible for focusing
options.B: Pumping blood vessels across the inner retina
options.C: Absorbing light photons to trigger an electrical signal
options.D: Lubricating the outer surface of the eyeball

explanation: Rhodopsin is the light-sensitive pigment that kicks off the nerve signals when light hits your rods in the dark.

question: Calcium, potassium, and iron belong to which group of nutrients?

options.A: Carbohydrates
options.B: Vitamins
options.C: Minerals
options.D: Proteins

explanation: These are essential minerals! They help build strong bones, balance your body fluids, and carry oxygen in your blood.

question: Which health history complaint needs an urgent neurological check right away?

options.A: Occasional muscle cramps after heavy exercise
options.B: Sudden changes in speech and vision
options.C: Temporary skin dryness in cold weather
options.D: Mild fatigue after a full night of sleep

explanation: Sudden trouble talking or seeing are major warning signs for a stroke or another urgent brain emergency. Always stay alert for these!

question: When would a nurse researcher choose a qualitative design?

options.A: To test a specific drug dosage on a group of people
options.B: To prove cause and effect using large numerical samples
options.C: To quickly measure blood pressure across a large population
options.D: To explore the emotional details of a patient's illness

explanation: Great thinking! We use qualitative designs when we want rich, descriptive stories about human experiences instead of cold numbers.

question: How do strict professional hierarchies sometimes hurt patient care?

options.A: They discourage junior staff and nurses from sharing critical patient observations
options.B: They ensure that every single medication is administered twice as fast
options.C: They eliminate all forms of communication errors between departments
options.D: They force patients to pay less money for hospital admission fees

explanation: Spot on! When junior staff or nurses feel intimidated by strict ranks, they might hold back life-saving observations out of fear.

question: By what age does a typical infant double their birth weight?

options.A: Six months
options.B: Nine months
options.C: Three months
options.D: Twelve months

explanation: Infants generally double their birth weight by six months of age and triple it by twelve months. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T12#GNS324_U3_T12_h2)

question: What is the medical term for a resting heart rate that stays above 100 beats per minute?

options.A: Bradycardia
options.B: Asystole
options.C: Arrhythmia
options.D: Tachycardia

explanation: Tachy- means fast! So when a resting heart rate races above 100 beats per minute, we call it tachycardia.

question: What is the usual gas flow rate range set on the flowmeter for a standard compressor nebulizer?

options.A: 20 to 25 liters per minute
options.B: 12 to 15 liters per minute
options.C: 6 to 8 liters per minute
options.D: 1 to 2 liters per minute

explanation: A flow rate of 6 to 8 liters per minute provides enough pressure to turn the liquid medicine into a proper mist. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h4)

question: In the famous '4 Ts' mnemonic for the causes of postpartum haemorrhage, what does the very first 'T' stand for?

options.A: Traction
options.B: Tone
options.C: Tachycardia
options.D: Temperature

explanation: Tone refers to uterine atony (when the uterus doesn't contract well). This is actually the number one cause of PPH you will see in the wards!

question: A student spends 12 hours a day playing online games, skips meals, and is failing exams. What does this point to?

options.A: Internet Gaming Disorder
options.B: Acute social anxiety
options.C: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder
options.D: Normal adolescent recreation

explanation: When gaming takes over someone's entire life and basic needs or responsibilities get ignored, it goes way beyond normal fun and fits Internet Gaming Disorder.

question: What is a helpful technique when a Parkinson's patient suddenly 'freezes' and cannot move their feet while walking?

options.A: Firmly push the patient forward from behind to restart momentum
options.B: Instruct the patient to lean backward to shift their center of gravity
options.C: Tell the patient to close their eyes and try to run quickly
options.D: Ask the patient to step over a visual cue on the floor or count out loud

explanation: Freezing can be scary! Using a visual trick—like stepping over a line on the floor—or counting a steady rhythm gives the brain a new cue to help break the freeze.

question: A patient is admitted with poorly controlled high blood pressure and fluid retention. The nurse provides counselling on a low-sodium diet. What type of counselling is this?

options.A: Preventive workplace wellness talks
options.B: Therapeutic and clinical counselling
options.C: General group weight-loss classes
options.D: Basic community nutrition outreach

explanation: Using a low-sodium diet to treat an active disease state like hypertension falls directly under clinical and therapeutic care. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T002#GNS227_U7_T002_h4)

question: What is a key nursing action when a dying patient is experiencing spiritual distress?

options.A: Ignore the comments because physical comfort is the only priority
options.B: Arrange a visit from a spiritual leader who matches the patient's beliefs
options.C: Convince the patient to adopt your own personal religious philosophy
options.D: Administer a sedative medication to calm the patient's anxious mind

explanation: Holistic care means caring for the spirit too. Connecting them with someone who shares their faith brings great peace.

question: In which of these situations would passing an NG tube through the nose be a huge NO-GO (contraindication)?

options.A: History of controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus
options.B: Localized skin infection on the lower leg
options.C: Mild chronic hypertension managed with medication
options.D: Severe facial trauma with a suspected skull fracture

explanation: Spotting a skull fracture means you never want to push anything through the nose—otherwise, the tube could accidentally find its way into the brain! Safety first.

question: When a patient has 'dysphagia', what exact trouble are they experiencing?

options.A: Frequent vomiting
options.B: Severe stomach pain
options.C: Involuntary weight loss
options.D: Difficulty swallowing

explanation: You've got this! Dysphagia is just the medical word for trouble or pain when swallowing food or drinks. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h2)

question: How does chloride rushing into brain cells help calm the nervous system?

options.A: It blocks the release of oxygen from nearby red blood cells
options.B: It depolarizes the cell membrane to speed up reflex pathways
options.C: It stops the production of cellular energy molecules in mitochondria
options.D: It hyperpolarizes the cell membrane, making electrical firing less likely

explanation: When negative chloride ions flood the inside of the cell, it becomes 'hyperpolarized'—meaning it's much harder for runaway electrical signals to trigger it.

question: Which waste product in a U&E panel comes directly from normal muscle breakdown?

options.A: Albumin
options.B: Urea
options.C: Bicarbonate
options.D: Creatinine

explanation: Well done! Creatinine is a natural byproduct of your everyday muscle activity that healthy kidneys filter right out of the blood.

question: When would a researcher prefer to use 'incidence density' instead of cumulative incidence?

options.A: When every single person stays in the study until the end
options.B: When calculating the prevalence of a permanent birth defect
options.C: When study participants enter at different times or drop out
options.D: When the researcher only cares about counting total deaths

explanation: Incidence density uses person-time, which is a lifesaver when people join a study at different times or drop out along the way.

question: A patient is receiving an anti-bleeding infusion. What is the most critical thing for the nurse to keep watching for?

options.A: Testing urine sugar levels after every meal
options.B: Watching for signs of abnormal blood clots and ongoing bleeding
options.C: Checking their eyesight every two hours
options.D: Checking daily weight changes for fluid retention

explanation: As a nurse, you walk a fine line: you want to make sure the bleeding stops, but you also must watch closely for signs of dangerous new clots forming!

question: What is a major difference between cancellous bone and compact bone?

options.A: Cancellous bone contains a network of trabeculae instead of dense osteons.
options.B: Compact bone contains active red marrow inside its matrix.
options.C: Cancellous bone has no blood supply running through it.
options.D: Compact bone lacks any living bone cells.

explanation: While compact bone is built out of tightly packed units called osteons, cancellous bone is built like an open web of tiny branching plates called trabeculae.

question: What happens inside the chest cavity when the diaphragm muscle contracts during inhalation?

options.A: Chest volume increases and air is pulled inward
options.B: The lungs collapse due to increased internal pressure
options.C: Chest volume decreases and air is pushed outward
options.D: Air pressure inside the lungs becomes higher than outside

explanation: Contracting the diaphragm flattens it out, making the chest cavity bigger and creating a vacuum that draws air into the lungs. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T4#GNS212_U2_T4_h1)

question: What is the primary purpose of placing a stockinette under a cast?

options.A: To cure the underlying bone fracture quickly
options.B: To protect the skin from rough casting materials
options.C: To add extra weight to the broken limb
options.D: To make the cast dry much faster in the sun

explanation: The stockinette acts as a soft barrier preventing harsh plaster or fiberglass from rubbing directly against the patient's skin. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h2)

question: What happens to the tiny coronary blood vessels when local waste products like adenosine pile up?

options.A: They constrict to stop bleeding.
options.B: They harden into rigid fibrous tubes.
options.C: They collapse from high pressure.
options.D: They dilate to increase blood flow.

explanation: Well done! Metabolic waste acts like a chemical green light, telling the blood vessels to relax and open wide so more oxygen can reach hardworking tissues.

question: In nursing, what does the term 'polypharmacy' mean?

options.A: Using a machine to deliver intravenous fluids
options.B: Taking multiple medications at the same time
options.C: Receiving treatment in a private hospital room
options.D: Having a severe allergy to common antibiotics

explanation: Polypharmacy simply means taking many drugs at once. This often increases the risk of side effects and drug clashes, so nurses have to monitor these patients closely.

question: A patient develops a painful, swollen, pus-filled lump at an injection site a few days after treatment. What is this likely a sign of?

options.A: A mild allergic reaction to clean cotton wool
options.B: An expected systemic reaction to vitamin supplements
options.C: A local bacterial infection and abscess formation
options.D: The normal healing process of deep muscle tissue

explanation: Ouch! When unsterile equipment or poor technique introduces bacteria into the tissue, it causes localized inflammation and can form a nasty abscess.

question: If a patient has a leaky heart valve that lets blood flow backward, what main change happens to that heart chamber?

options.A: Instant muscle atrophy
options.B: Volume overload and chamber dilation
options.C: Complete electrical shutdown
options.D: Immediate valve healing

explanation: A leaky valve means extra blood flows backward into the chamber. This extra volume stretches and enlarges (dilates) the heart muscle over time.

question: Why do healthcare decisions often involve political negotiation?

options.A: Medical equipment never breaks down unexpectedly
options.B: Resources are limited and demand is high
options.C: Doctors refuse to speak with government officials
options.D: Patients prefer traditional healers to hospitals

explanation: Scarcity forces leaders to make tough choices about where money and support go, which requires political bargaining. [learn more](GST321_U6_T3#GST321_U6_T3_h1)

question: Which lab value or vital sign must be checked regularly for patients on long-term corticosteroids?

options.A: Liver enzyme AST
options.B: Blood glucose levels
options.C: Red blood cell count
options.D: Serum creatinine

explanation: Correct! Steroids trigger the liver to release stored sugar, which often leads to high blood sugar levels that need close monitoring.

question: Which technology helps link patient prescriptions directly with pharmacy dispensing software?

options.A: Manual paper ledgers stored in wooden cabinets
options.B: Electronic health records and barcoding systems
options.C: Standard telephone landlines on the ward
options.D: Traditional wall clocks placed in the hallway

explanation: Digital records and barcode scanners speed up order transmission and reduce transcription mistakes between departments. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h8)

question: What is the main goal of debulking surgery for ovarian cancer?

options.A: To preserve the uterus and ovaries for future childbearing
options.B: To completely cure the patient without needing chemotherapy
options.C: To remove as much visible tumor mass from the abdomen as possible
options.D: To eliminate the need for any follow-up blood tests

explanation: Spot on! Leaving behind as little tumor as possible makes the follow-up chemotherapy much more effective.

question: What does a smoking history measurement called 'pack-years' calculate?

options.A: The number of years the person has completely stopped smoking
options.B: The number of packs smoked per day multiplied by years smoked
options.C: The total financial cost of cigarettes over a lifetime
options.D: The average age the client started smoking daily

explanation: Pack-years give a clear numerical value of a person's total tobacco exposure over time, which helps assess chronic lung disease risk. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T2#GNS213_U2_T2_h2)

question: The ultimate goal of inter-professional collaboration supported by assertiveness is...

options.A: faster completion of paperwork shifts
options.B: fewer meetings for senior managers
options.C: safer and more effective patient care
options.D: lower hospital electricity bills

explanation: Clear teamwork across different health professions directly results in safer outcomes for the patient. [learn more](GST321_U7_T5#GST321_U7_T5_h6)

question: What factor most commonly drives teenagers toward dangerous, underground abortion practices?

options.A: Abundant availability of free clinical termination services
options.B: Encouragement from community health committees
options.C: Complete legal protection for all medical procedures
options.D: Strict social stigma, legal restrictions, and lack of safe care access

explanation: Exactly. When judgment, strict laws, and a lack of open support block safe care, desperate teenagers unfortunately turn to risky alternatives.

question: Why does a ventilation-perfusion mismatch happen when someone has a severe lung infection?

options.A: Blocked air sacs still get blood flow, but can't get fresh air.
options.B: The throat swells up and stops breathing completely.
options.C: The heart pumps blood way too slowly for the lungs.
options.D: Mucus plugs in the windpipe block blood from reaching the heart.

explanation: Think of it as a mismatch: blood is flowing past the air sacs ready to pick up oxygen, but because they are full of fluid, there's no fresh air waiting for them.

question: What official list guides healthcare workers on which medicines are approved for public health facilities?

options.A: Essential Medicines List
options.B: Standard Nursing Care Plan
options.C: Global Import Tariff Book
options.D: Private Pharmacy Catalog

explanation: Well done! The Essential Medicines List (EML) contains the carefully selected drugs needed to meet the priority healthcare needs of the community.

question: Which form of a drug molecule passes most easily across biological cell membranes?

options.A: Ionized
options.B: Conjugated
options.C: Unionized
options.D: Protein-bound

explanation: Unionized (un-charged) drug molecules are more fat-friendly (lipophilic), helping them slip smoothly across cell membranes.

question: A community health nurse is talking to abattoir (slaughterhouse) workers about their daily risks. Which animal-borne diseases should be the main focus?

options.A: Cerebrospinal meningitis
options.B: Cholera and typhoid fever
options.C: Anthrax and brucellosis
options.D: Malaria and yellow fever

explanation: You nailed it! Because abattoir workers handle livestock directly, they are at higher risk for zoonotic infections like anthrax and brucellosis.

question: Which of these is NOT a common sign of family dysfunction or distress?

options.A: Young children forced into premature caregiving roles
options.B: Open, respectful communication and shared problem-solving
options.C: Unresolved domestic violence and persistent household conflict
options.D: Severe social isolation from neighbors

explanation: Open communication and teamwork are signs of a healthy, happy family, not a dysfunctional one!

question: A nurse uses a video call to inspect a healing surgical wound for an elderly patient at home. Which model of care does this represent?

options.A: Inpatient intensive care model
options.B: Home care nursing model
options.C: Pure administrative billing model
options.D: Emergency trauma surgery model

explanation: Using video visits to monitor recovery and wound healing at home falls under the home care tele-nursing model. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h3)

question: A patient had a deep cut on their shin stitched 8 days ago and asks to remove the stitches. What do you tell them?

options.A: Yes, because leg wounds heal faster than any other body part
options.B: Yes, all sutures can safely come out after exactly seven days
options.C: No, sutures must stay in place for at least a full month
options.D: No, limb and joint wounds usually need ten to fourteen days of healing support

explanation: Areas over joints or shins move a lot and have less blood flow, so they need 10 to 14 days before taking stitches out. Safety first!

question: Why does the radiographer take several X-ray pictures at different timed intervals during an IVP?

options.A: To track how the kidneys filter and pass the dye through the urinary tract
options.B: To expose the patient to different angles of radiation for safety checks
options.C: To measure how quickly the patient's blood pressure drops from the injection
options.D: To allow the contrast dye enough time to completely dissolve in the blood

explanation: Timed pictures act like a mini-movie, letting us watch in real-time as the kidneys catch the dye and drain it downward.

question: What is the main reason a doctor performs a skin biopsy?

options.A: To completely remove a large area of infected tissue
options.B: To obtain a tissue sample for microscopic examination
options.C: To drain purulent fluid from a deep subcutaneous abscess
options.D: To deliver topical medications directly to the dermis

explanation: You've got this! A skin biopsy simply means taking a tiny piece of skin so the lab can look at it closely under a microscope to figure out what's going on.

question: What is the main difference between meningitis and encephalitis?

options.A: Encephalitis is always caused by fungi, while meningitis is always caused by bacteria.
options.B: Meningitis causes personality changes, while encephalitis only causes stiff joints.
options.C: Meningitis affects the spinal cord exclusively, while encephalitis affects only the skull.
options.D: Encephalitis involves inflammation of the brain tissue itself, while meningitis affects the protective membranes around it.

explanation: Meningitis targets the 'meninges' (the covering layers), while encephalitis targets the actual 'encephalon' (the brain tissue itself). Simple and easy to remember!

question: What equipment provides the gold standard for sterilizing surgical instruments using moist heat?

options.A: Hot air oven
options.B: Pressure cooker
options.C: Autoclave
options.D: Boiling water bath

explanation: The autoclave uses pressurized steam to achieve temperatures high enough to kill bacterial spores effectively. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h2)

question: What happens during drug distribution in the body?

options.A: The liver breaks down the medicine into waste products
options.B: The gut absorbs a swallowed pill
options.C: The drug moves from the blood into various body tissues
options.D: The kidneys eliminate active drug molecules

explanation: Think of distribution as the drug's journey out of the bloodstream and into the body tissues where it's actually needed to work! You've got this.

question: Which factor is most important for keeping a DRF cycle running successfully for years?

options.A: Strict financial discipline and accurate inventory monitoring
options.B: Relying exclusively on large, unpredictable international donations
options.C: Stopping all forms of health insurance participation in the hospital
options.D: Selling all essential medicines at extremely high commercial markups

explanation: You got it! Good bookkeeping, careful stock checks, and making sure money always finds its way back to inventory are the real keys to success.

question: How do condoms stop sexually transmitted infections from spreading between partners?

options.A: Antibiotics coated on the inside of the sheath
options.B: Chemical destruction of bacteria by latex proteins
options.C: A physical barrier blocking contact with infectious fluids
options.D: Immune system stimulation from the lubricant

explanation: Spot on! The material creates a solid wall so infectious fluids never touch or enter mucous membranes.

question: An elderly patient with several chronic diseases and memory issues is admitted to the ward. Who is best suited to lead their medical care?

options.A: A surgical resident
options.B: A hospital pharmacist
options.C: A physical therapist
options.D: A geriatrician

explanation: Geriatricians are experts at balancing complex medications and multiple health conditions specifically for older patients.

question: Which of these tasks is NOT part of a nurse's daily responsibilities when dealing with LFTs?

options.A: Monitoring the blood draw site for bleeding afterward
options.B: Diagnosing the specific stage of cirrhosis from the lab slip
options.C: Ensuring proper patient preparation and fasting if required
options.D: Checking patient medication history for drugs that stress the liver

explanation: That's right! We prep the patient, check medications, and keep them safe, but making the final disease diagnosis is the doctor's job.

question: Why must you check IV lines and power cords before adjusting a smart bed's position?

options.A: To prevent lines from becoming pinched or disconnected during articulation
options.B: To ensure the bed connects properly to the central hospital Wi-Fi
options.C: To prevent the bed's built-in scale from registering incorrect weights
options.D: To keep the floor clear so housekeeping can mop underneath

explanation: As the bed moves up or down, it can easily pull or snap tight IV lines and oxygen tubing if you haven't checked them first.

question: What does the abbreviation 'gtt' mean in medication administration?

options.A: Gallon
options.B: Dose
options.C: Gram
options.D: Drop

explanation: You nailed it! 'gtt' comes from 'gutta', the Latin word for a drop. You'll spot this when calculating IV drips or giving eye drops.

question: What happens inside the blood vessels when you apply heat to a patient's skin?

options.A: Complete occlusion
options.B: Vasodilation
options.C: Instant calcification
options.D: Vasoconstriction

explanation: Think of heat as opening up the pipes! It causes vasodilation (widening of the blood vessels), which brings more rich blood circulation straight to the area.

question: What is the normal blood pH range for a healthy human body?
explanation: Think of 7.35 to 7.45 as the body's sweet spot. Keeping blood slightly alkaline here keeps all our cells and enzymes happy and working smoothly.

question: Why does a baby with Tetralogy of Fallot sometimes turn very blue when crying?

options.A: The lungs suddenly fill with large amounts of clear fluid.
options.B: Deoxygenated blood mixes and enters the systemic circulation.
options.C: The heart stops beating completely for several minutes.
options.D: Blood flow to the brain increases too quickly.

explanation: Because of the heart defects in Tetralogy of Fallot, oxygen-poor blood bypasses the lungs and goes straight out to the body, giving the skin a bluish tint.

question: What is the most frequent cause of an overactive thyroid (hyperthyroidism)?

options.A: Severe iodine deficiency
options.B: Graves' disease
options.C: Pituitary adenoma
options.D: Hashimoto's thyroiditis

explanation: Spot on! Graves' disease is an autoimmune issue where stimulating antibodies trick the thyroid into working overtime.

question: Which action is considered the single most effective way to prevent the spread of infections in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Keeping windows closed at night
options.B: Painting isolation walls white
options.C: Frequent and proper hand hygiene
options.D: Changing bed sheets twice a day

explanation: Handwashing with soap and water or using alcohol-based rub removes pathogens from hands before they spread to others. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h7)

question: A clinical instructor grades a student differently today just because they are in a bad mood. Which core principle is broken here?

options.A: Validity
options.B: Usability
options.C: Objectivity
options.D: Comprehensiveness

explanation: Objectivity means grading fairly based on facts, not personal feelings or moods. Nobody likes a grumpy marker!

question: Which of these is NOT a common risk factor for stress urinary incontinence?

options.A: Obesity and excess body weight
options.B: Menopause and decreased estrogen levels
options.C: Frequent high-fluid intake throughout the day
options.D: Vaginal childbirth and multiple pregnancies

explanation: Drinking plenty of water is healthy! The real risk factors involve things that weaken pelvic support, like childbirth, hormonal shifts, or heavy pressure.

question: How many pairs of cranial nerves do we have in our body?

options.A: Twenty-four pairs
options.B: Twelve pairs
options.C: Ten pairs
options.D: Thirty-one pairs

explanation: You've got this! There are 12 pairs of cranial nerves coming straight from the brain to help manage our head, neck, and organs.

question: A patient with a fresh neck injury suddenly has dangerously low blood pressure and zero reflexes. What is this temporary condition called?

options.A: Renal failure
options.B: Cerebral edema
options.C: Tetraplegic fever
options.D: Spinal shock

explanation: Spot on! Spinal shock happens right after a severe spinal cord injury. The cord basically goes to 'sleep' temporarily, causing a sudden loss of all reflexes and muscle tone below the injury site.

question: Which cranial nerve are you testing when you shine a penlight into a patient's eyes to check their pupils?

options.A: Cranial nerve I
options.B: Cranial nerve XII
options.C: Cranial nerve III
options.D: Cranial nerve VIII

explanation: Cranial nerve III (the oculomotor nerve) handles pupillary constriction. It's a quick reflex test you'll do all the time in clinicals!

question: What is a very common emotional experience for patients facing the end of their lives?

options.A: Existential distress and questioning life meaning
options.B: An intense desire to run marathons
options.C: Complete indifference to surroundings and people
options.D: Sudden loss of all emotional feelings

explanation: You got it! Toward the end of life, it's completely normal for patients to look back, wonder about their life's purpose, and work through big deep questions.

question: How do epidermal inclusion cysts typically form on the vulva?

options.A: Blocked sweat glands swell up during hot weather conditions
options.B: Surface skin cells get trapped beneath the skin after trauma or surgery
options.C: Embryonic remnants fill with fluid during puberty development
options.D: Infected hair follicles burst open and trap blood underneath

explanation: Sometimes, after an episiotomy, minor injury, or surgery, surface skin cells get pushed deeper under the tissue where they form a little fluid pocket.

question: What is a super important piece of discharge teaching for a patient on antibiotics for a bone infection?

options.A: Switch to topical creams once the IV line is removed
options.B: Stop taking the drugs the moment pain subsides
options.C: Double the dose if a fever returns for one evening
options.D: Finish the entire prescription even if symptoms disappear

explanation: Always remind patients to finish every single pill! Stopping early can let the stubborn bacteria bounce back stronger.

question: What is the best move when a grateful patient offers you an expensive gift?

options.A: Accept it gladly as a reward for hard work
options.B: Politely decline, explaining agency policy on gifts
options.C: Suggest the patient give cash instead of an item
options.D: Accept it secretly so other staff members do not get jealous

explanation: Great job! Accepting pricey gifts can mess with your professional objectivity. A kind, polite 'thank you, but I can't accept this' protects your integrity.

question: What is a major dual benefit of school feeding programs?

options.A: Reducing the operational costs of running public schools
options.B: Improving child nutrition and boosting school attendance
options.C: Training children to become professional commercial farmers
options.D: Eliminating the need for children to ever visit a doctor

explanation: School meals fight hunger while giving families an extra incentive to keep children in school. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h6)

question: Why is intersectoral collaboration important in primary health care?

options.A: It allows doctors to control local government policies
options.B: It ensures that hospitals make a higher financial profit
options.C: Health is influenced by factors like food, education, and housing, not just medicine
options.D: It stops nurses from having to do any home visits

explanation: Because health depends on social determinants like clean water, education, and nutrition, health sectors must work alongside agriculture, education, and public works. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h2)

question: How are benign tumors different from malignant ones?

options.A: Benign tumors cannot grow larger than a few millimeters.
options.B: Benign tumors only occur in the blood and lymphatic system.
options.C: Benign tumors do not invade nearby tissues or spread to distant sites.
options.D: Benign tumors consist of dead cells rather than dividing cells.

explanation: Think of benign tumors as staying put in one place without invading surrounding tissues. They aren't cancerous like malignant ones!

question: How does the nurse-patient relationship in a geriatric home usually differ from an acute care hospital?

options.A: It requires no communication with family members
options.B: It focuses exclusively on surgical recovery
options.C: It involves only one-time emergency interventions
options.D: It is typically long-term and relationship-focused

explanation: Because care lasts months or years, nurses get to build warm, lasting relationships with the residents. It is one of the most rewarding parts of nursing!

question: At what stage of life is a child's physical growth speed (velocity) at its absolute highest?

options.A: Toddler years
options.B: Early adolescence
options.C: Middle childhood
options.D: Infancy

explanation: Babies grow faster than at any other time in their lives! That rapid change is why infants need so much energy and good nutrition packed into their tiny bodies.

question: What is moulding in the context of labour?

options.A: The stretching of the lower uterine segment during the second stage of labour
options.B: The natural softening of the cervix before active contractions begin
options.C: The abnormal swelling of the baby's scalp caused by pressure
options.D: The shifting and overlapping of fetal skull bones to fit through the pelvis

explanation: Moulding is the medical term for the overlapping of the baby's skull plates to reduce head size during birth. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T14#GNS121_U6_T14_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a standard nursing check after a contrast CT scan?

options.A: Evaluating baseline lung sounds for sudden fluid overload
options.B: Checking the intravenous site for swelling or leakage
options.C: Monitoring the patient for delayed allergic rashes
options.D: Encouraging the patient to drink plenty of fluids

explanation: Unless there's a specific heart or kidney issue, checking lung sounds isn't part of routine post-CT care. But checking the IV site, watching for rashes, and pushing fluids definitely are!

question: What is a primary responsibility of nurses when they suspect a patient is a victim of forced marriage?

options.A: Confronting the spouse aggressively in the waiting room
options.B: Ignoring the situation to maintain patient confidentiality strictly
options.C: Discharging the patient immediately without documentation
options.D: Providing a safe, private space to assess for abuse and offer resources

explanation: Nurses must create a confidential environment to talk with the patient alone, evaluate safety, and connect them with support services. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T14#GNS312_U1_T14_h5)

question: Six hours after delivery, a mom feels dizzy. You check and find her uterus is soft (boggy) and pushed to the right. What is your immediate nursing action?

options.A: Prepare the patient for immediate major surgery
options.B: Massage the uterine fundus until firm and encourage bladder emptying
options.C: Administer oral pain relievers and tell her to sleep
options.D: Check her blood glucose level and offer juice

explanation: A boggy uterus means it's relaxing and bleeding could start! Massaging it helps it contract, and getting her to empty her bladder will stop it from being pushed out of place.

question: Which behavior strongly suggests that a patient is dealing with high emotional stress?

options.A: Slow, deep, and regular breathing
options.B: Withdrawal and tearfulness
options.C: Eager participation in daily planning
options.D: Relaxed facial muscles and posture

explanation: When people feel overwhelmed emotionally, they often shut down, pull away from others, or break down in tears. Keep an eye out for these cues as a nurse! [learn more](GNS123_U3_T15#GNS123_U3_T15_h5)

question: What is the primary trigger for a cardiac action potential across cell membranes?

options.A: Movement of ions like sodium and potassium
options.B: Release of stored oxygen molecules in the tissue
options.C: Sudden changes in the temperature of the blood
options.D: Direct stimulation by circulating red blood cells

explanation: Cardiac cells generate electrical activity by rapidly shifting ions like sodium, potassium, and calcium across their membranes. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h1)

question: What is the main difference between primary and secondary skin lesions?

options.A: Primary lesions require surgical removal, while secondary lesions always resolve without any intervention
options.B: Primary lesions only appear on the face, while secondary lesions are found exclusively on the lower extremities
options.C: Primary lesions are always painless, whereas secondary lesions always cause severe systemic fever
options.D: Primary lesions develop directly from the disease process, while secondary ones result from changes like scratching or healing

explanation: You got it! Primary lesions pop up straight from the illness itself, while secondary ones form later due to things like scratching or scabbing.

question: What is the true purpose of writing a hospital incident report?

options.A: It is used for quality improvement and learning from system flaws
options.B: It serves as a formal legal tool to discipline negligent nurses
options.C: It is placed permanently in the patient's bedside clinical chart
options.D: It is required by insurance companies to calculate hospital bills

explanation: Incident reports are confidential tools meant to help the hospital figure out what went wrong in the system so safety can be improved for everyone. It's about fixing the system, not witch-hunting!

question: A patient with terminal cancer talks about missing her daughter's wedding next year. What type of grief is this?

options.A: Exaggerated grief
options.B: Anticipatory grief
options.C: Collective grief
options.D: Disenfranchised grief

explanation: Spot on! Mourning future events or losses before they actually take place is a clear sign of anticipatory grief. Great clinical thinking!

question: What is a major hygiene worry for an infant in Gallows traction?

options.A: Urine and stool getting on the traction tapes and skin
options.B: Food clogging the metal pulleys
options.C: Saliva causing chest skin breakdown
options.D: Sweating causing quick dehydration

explanation: With the baby's hips up in the air and wearing a diaper in a tight spot, leaks happen. Keeping this area clean is a major nursing duty to stop infections!

question: When is the best time to initiate breastfeeding after an uncomplicated delivery?

options.A: Within the first hour of birth
options.B: Once the milk transitions to white
options.C: After twenty-four hours of rest
options.D: After the baby receives initial vaccines

explanation: Starting breastfeeding within the first hour takes advantage of the baby's alert state and helps milk production start smoothly. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h5)

question: What does cervical mucus look and feel like right around the time of ovulation?

options.A: Thin and watery with a strong foul odor
options.B: Dry, crumbly, and dark brown in color
options.C: Clear, stretchy, and slippery like raw egg whites
options.D: Thick, sticky, and opaque like paste

explanation: High estrogen makes fertile mucus stretchy and slippery—just like raw egg white—to help sperm swim up easily. Nature is amazing!

question: What is the main reason a doctor performs a fine-needle aspiration (FNA) biopsy on a thyroid lump?

options.A: To obtain cells for microscopic examination to check for cancer
options.B: To inject radioactive isotopes directly into the thyroid tissue
options.C: To completely remove the entire thyroid gland without surgery
options.D: To measure the 24-hour baseline hormone production levels

explanation: Spot on! An FNA takes a tiny sample of cells so the lab can check them under a microscope to confirm or rule out cancer.

question: When should the rehabilitation journey ideally start for a patient who has suffered a major injury?

options.A: When the patient asks to start walking
options.B: Only after the patient is discharged home
options.C: As soon as the patient is medically stable
options.D: After all chronic complications develop

explanation: Rehab starts early—right after the patient is medically stable—to prevent stiffness and get a head start on recovery.

question: Who belongs in an isolation ward rather than a quarantine area?

options.A: Persons who are already sick with confirmed active symptoms
options.B: Community members who missed their routine vaccination
options.C: Family members living in the same house as a sick patient
options.D: Healthy travelers arriving from a country with an ongoing outbreak

explanation: Isolation is specifically reserved for individuals who are currently ill with a contagious disease. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h2)

question: Why do nurses sometimes hesitate to ask patients about their spiritual needs?

options.A: Lack of available paperwork charts in the nursing station
options.B: Patients always refuse to answer questions about faith
options.C: Fear of imposing personal values or causing offense
options.D: Strict hospital policies forbidding any talk of religion

explanation: It's totally normal to worry about crossing boundaries, but being gentle and respectful makes spiritual care safe and meaningful for the patient.

question: What acid-base imbalance can develop from continuous stomach suctioning?

options.A: Metabolic acidosis
options.B: Respiratory acidosis
options.C: Metabolic alkalosis
options.D: Respiratory alkalosis

explanation: Sucking out large amounts of acidic stomach fluid leaves the body with excess base, leading to metabolic alkalosis. You're mastering body chemistry!

question: During which week of enteric fever are dangerous complications like intestinal bleeding or tears most likely to happen?

options.A: Eighth week
options.B: Third week
options.C: Fifth week
options.D: First week

explanation: Spot on! By the third week, intestinal tissues have taken a heavy beating, raising the risk of bleeding or holes in the bowel.

question: Why do low-income households frequently purchase highly processed foods?

options.A: Government food programs forbid buying fresh produce
options.B: They provide cheap calories that quickly relieve hunger
options.C: They contain more vitamins than fresh vegetables
options.D: They spoil much slower than natural foods

explanation: Processed foods packed with sugar and fat are inexpensive and filling, making them an economical choice for families with tight budgets. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T020#GNS227_U2_T020_h2)

question: What is one of the earliest signs that the brain is not getting enough oxygen during shock?

options.A: Restlessness and anxiety
options.B: Slurred speech patterns
options.C: Sudden memory loss
options.D: Deep unresponsiveness

explanation: The brain is very sensitive to oxygen! Long before blood pressure crashes, a patient will often start acting anxious, restless, or confused simply because their brain cells are thirsty for oxygen.

question: Where are ganglia located in the human body?

options.A: Within the center of the spinal cord
options.B: Outside the central nervous system
options.C: Directly on skeletal muscle fibers
options.D: Inside the cerebral cortex only

explanation: You can picture ganglia as little relay stations located out in the peripheral nervous system, away from the brain and spinal cord.

question: A nurse hands a patient their morning pills, but the patient is busy talking on the phone and asks the nurse to leave the cup on the bedside table. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Place the pills in the patient's water cup so they dissolve for later
options.B: Take the pills away and document that the patient refused the medication
options.C: Leave the pills on the table and remind the nurse's assistant to check later
options.D: Stay with the patient, wait until they finish the call, and watch them take the pills

explanation: Medications should never be left unattended at the bedside because the patient might forget them, take them incorrectly, or someone else might take them. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h6)

question: What is a normal capillary refill time when you press on a healthy adult's nail bed?

options.A: Less than two seconds
options.B: More than fifteen seconds
options.C: Exactly five to six seconds
options.D: Up to ten full seconds

explanation: Brisk is best! When you press a nail bed and let go, good blood flow should bring the pink color back in under two seconds.

question: When monitoring vital signs in a patient with suspected internal bleeding, what is most important to look for?

options.A: A single normal blood pressure reading
options.B: A sudden drop in body temperature
options.C: An increase in respiratory depth only
options.D: Trends indicating a worsening condition over time

explanation: Observing how vital signs change sequentially gives a much clearer picture of ongoing blood loss than looking at one isolated set of numbers. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T2#GNS112_U7_T2_h4)

question: How can nurses help stop community members from hiding infectious illnesses out of fear?

options.A: Refusing to treat patients who do not speak English
options.B: Keeping all health information secret from local leaders
options.C: Threatening penalties for families that miss immunization days
options.D: Building trust through health education and supportive care

explanation: When we show empathy, educate gently, and create a safe space without judgment, community members feel comfortable coming to us early.

question: What is the final goal of the complement cascade when attacking a bacterium?

options.A: Thickening of the local epithelial basement membrane
options.B: Production of specific IgE antibodies against the bacterial wall
options.C: Maturation of naive T-cells into active helper cells
options.D: Formation of a membrane attack complex that lyses the cell

explanation: You got it! The complement system builds a 'membrane attack complex' that drills holes in the germ until it bursts (lyses).

question: Which glands add fluid to semen as it travels along the reproductive tract?

options.A: Sweat glands and sebaceous glands
options.B: Thyroid gland and pituitary gland
options.C: Seminal vesicles and prostate gland
options.D: Adrenal glands and pancreas

question: Where in the brain is the main control center for the cough reflex located?

options.A: Cerebellum
options.B: Spinal cord
options.C: Frontal lobe
options.D: Medulla oblongata

explanation: The medulla oblongata is the brainstem command center that coordinates the whole physical action of coughing.

question: Which PHC principle ensures that rural and underserved populations get a fair share of health services?

options.A: Tertiary specialization
options.B: Technological centralization
options.C: Equitable distribution
options.D: Commercial privatization

explanation: Equitable distribution simply means fairness—making sure health resources reach everyone, especially vulnerable groups who need them most.

question: What should a caregiver do first if a child swallows a toxic household cleaner?

options.A: Force the child to drink large amounts of milk
options.B: Wait to see if the child develops a cough
options.C: Call emergency services or poison control immediately
options.D: Make the child vomit right away to clear the stomach

question: Why is being kind and compassionate so important when caring for a PAC patient?

options.A: It prevents the physical pain caused by uterine contractions
options.B: It shortens the standard hospital stay to less than two hours
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for any antibiotic therapy
options.D: It reduces anxiety and encourages honest disclosure of medical history

explanation: When patients feel safe and free from judgment, they are much more likely to share true details that help us care for them better.
